text.title: Readiness Checklist Decision Tree
text.summary: Lifecycle-position gate first, then preconditions, then the git diff decides which conditional items apply. Routes to run / a specific item rule / skip; every conclusion references a rule id from 01-core-rules.xml.

decision-tree.root-question: Is the feature in `features/in-progress/F0NN-slug/` and does the developer believe it is done?

branch.question: Are the preconditions present? (SDD lifecycle features/{backlog,todo,in-progress,done} in use AND CI configured with lint + typecheck + unit)

branch.conclusion: Skip; surface the missing precondition. Item 4 cannot be evaluated without CI.

branch.question: What does the git diff touch? (the diff decides, not the developer's assessment of scope)

branch.conclusion: Item 5 applies: API tests must pass and be linked as evidence.
Item 6 applies: at least one positive AND one negative Playwright case per flow.
Item 7 applies: documented Nielsen 5 + Norman 2 audit in ui-ux-design.md.
Grep sibling surfaces in the same namespace and document the result in readiness.md.

branch.when: backend_source_tree_changed == false AND user_facing_flow == false AND visible_ui_changed == false
branch.conclusion: Run the procedure; items 5–7 are not-applicable with a reason, items 1–4 and 8–10 always apply.
Empty boxes block the transition. Do not move to done/.

Skip: a sibling methodology is the better fit for the lifecycle position — sdd-promotion-gate-checklist for backlog→todo, cr-bug-tracking's lighter flow for a standalone CR; a throwaway prototype has no done/ target.

text.example: inputs: {position=in-progress, developer_claims_done=true, ci=true, diff: apps/billing/views.py} q-position -> true q-preconditions -> true q-diff -> backend_source_tree_changed=true, user_facing_flow=false, visible_ui_changed=false => conclusion i5-api-tests: item 5 applies; items 6, 7 not-applicable with reason. items 1-5, 8, 9 ticked with evidence; item 10 empty => conclusion gate-empty-box-blocks: verdict blocked until deployed.
